Deputy Fionntán Ó Súilleabháin asked the Minister for Further and Higher Education, Research, Innovation and Science the number of students studying occupational therapy, dietetics, physiotherapy, speech and language therapy, psychology and psychotherapy in each higher education institution, for each of the past five years; the number graduating annually from each discipline; the number of funded training places available in each year, in tabular form; whether a shortfall in graduates is contributing to HSE vacancies and extended waiting lists in disability and community services; and if he will make a statement on the matter. [63573/26]

questions.heading: Health Services
questions.question: 4008. Deputy Fionntán Ó Súilleabháin asked the Minister for Health if her attention has been drawn to the recent High Court judgment by Mr Justice Paul Coffey, which described the total absence of a coordinated care pathway for Huntington's disease (HD) in Ireland as "shameful" and "urgently required"; the reason the comprehensive proposal for a National HD Care Pathway submitted to the HSE by clinical experts and an organisation (details supplied) has not been implemented or funded; and if she will make a statement on this matter. [63571/26]

questions.heading: Health Services Staff
questions.question: 3990. Deputy Fionntán Ó Súilleabháin asked the Minister for Health if she is aware that Ireland has only one dedicated specialist HD nurse for the entire national population (details supplied); if she will contrast this lack of resources with the multi-disciplinary clinic networks available to the Motor Neurone Disease (MND) community in Ireland and HD families in Scotland; and if she will provide an immediate, definitive timeline for the establishment of specialist multidisciplinary clinics to ensure Irish HD patients have equal access to clinical trials and co-ordinated lifetime care. [63572/26]

questions.heading: Housing Policy
questions.question: 1963. Deputy Fionntán Ó Súilleabháin asked the Minister for Housing, Local Government and Heritage if he will address the structural trap facing middle-income households who earn above the social housing income limits but cannot bridge the deposit gap for new-build homes or access the first home scheme due to rapid market inflation; the measures his Department is taking to provide dedicated housing security and purchase pathways for long-term private renters in this specific bracket who are at risk of displacement; and if he will make a statement on the matter. [63579/26]

questions.heading: Housing Schemes
questions.question: 886. Deputy Fionntán Ó Súilleabháin asked the Tánaiste and Minister for Finance if he will review the eligibility criteria for the help to buy (HTB) incentive scheme, to address the exclusion of Irish citizens living permanently in the State who operate as cross-border workers, paying income tax in Northern Ireland but residing in the Republic of Ireland, who are currently disqualified from the scheme due to not having paid a minimum threshold of income tax or Deposit Interest Retention Tax (DIRT) directly within the jurisdiction over the preceding four years; and if he will make a statement on the matter. [63578/26]

questions.heading: Live Exports
questions.question: 2798. Deputy Fionntán Ó Súilleabháin asked the Minister for Agriculture, Food and the Marine the specific, measurable actions his Department is taking to identify, inspect and approve alternative vessel capacity ahead of the autumn weanling trade and next spring's calf export season; if he has engaged directly with alternative commercial ferry operators to ensure continuous access to the single market; and if he will make a statement on the matter. [63570/26]

questions.heading: Live Exports
questions.question: 2799. Deputy Fionntán Ó Súilleabháin asked the Minister for Agriculture, Food and the Marine if he will provide a full statistical breakdown of the total number of live cattle and calves exported from Ireland to date this year compared to the same period in 2025; the volume of these exports broken down by destination country; if his attention has been drawn to recent industry meetings in Athlone highlighting structural deficits in shipping infrastructure following the withdrawal of a service (details supplied) from transporting live animals; and if he will make a statement on the matter. [63569/26]

questions.heading: Local Authorities
questions.question: 1943. Deputy Fionntán Ó Súilleabháin asked the Minister for Housing, Local Government and Heritage the total number of staffing sanction requests submitted to his Department by each of the 31 local authorities for new or additional posts across all functional areas for the years 2024, 2025, and to date in 2026; the specific number of these requests that were approved, rejected, or are currently awaiting decision by his Department; the specific number of sanctions requested and granted for general outdoor maintenance and parks staff during this same period; and if he will make a statement on the matter. [63581/26]

questions.heading: Travel Documents
questions.question: 2629. Deputy Fionntán Ó Súilleabháin asked the Minister for Justice, Home Affairs and Migration whether exemptions will apply to residents of the North of Ireland under the new travel arrangements due to come into effect on 28 September 2026; the categories of persons who will be exempt; and if he will make a statement on the matter [63577/26]

questions.heading: Travel Documents
questions.question: 2630. Deputy Fionntán Ó Súilleabháin asked the Minister for Justice, Home Affairs and Migration if he will intervene following a decision (details supplied) to require all passengers travelling between Ireland and Great Britain to present a valid passport from 28 September 2026 due to changes being introduced to comply with UK Border Force data requirements; whether he has received legal advice on whether this requirement is compatible with the Common Travel Area Agreement; and if he will make a statement on this matter. [63576/26]

questions.heading: Airport Security
questions.question: 339. Deputy Malcolm Byrne asked the Minister for Transport the measures in place to prevent potential drone attacks at Irish airports. [61293/26]

questions.heading: Animal Feedstuffs
questions.question: 2662. Deputy Malcolm Byrne asked the Minister for Agriculture, Food and the Marine if there are plans to provide supports, including capital funding, for the development of an organic feed mill. [60432/26]

questions.heading: Artificial Intelligence
questions.question: 1011. Deputy Malcolm Byrne asked the Minister for Enterprise, Tourism and Employment if it is intended to establish a youth advisory panel within the new National Artificial Intelligence Office. [59852/26]

questions.heading: Arts Funding
questions.question: 1591. Deputy Malcolm Byrne asked the Minister for Culture, Communications and Sport the progress on the Programme for Government commitment to provide affordable spaces for artists to work and collaborate. [60463/26]

questions.heading: Arts Funding
questions.question: 1593. Deputy Malcolm Byrne asked the Minister for Culture, Communications and Sport the progress on the Programme for Government commitment to expand arts programming in early childhood education. [60476/26]

questions.heading: Bus Services
questions.question: 344. Deputy Malcolm Byrne asked the Minister for Transport the measures his Department has put in place to encourage the uptake of a career in bus driving; the supports available for driver training; and if he will make a statement on the matter. [61286/26]

questions.heading: Coast Guard Service
questions.question: 343. Deputy Malcolm Byrne asked the Minister for Transport the number of new coastguard stations built by the State in the period 2016 to 2025, inclusive; the total sum for each year of that period spent on design and planning works for all potential coastguard stations; and the total capital expenditure on coastguard stations for each of those years. [61290/26]

questions.heading: Coast Guard Service
questions.question: 394. Deputy Malcolm Byrne asked the Minister for Transport the number of new coastguard stations built by the State in each of the years 2016 to 2025; the total amount for each year of that period spent on design and planning works for all potential coastguard stations; and the total capital expenditure on coastguard stations in each of those years. [61591/26]
